_format: Slice 11a trace-ingestion ground truth, read by crates/nerve-index/tests/trace.rs.
Written BEFORE trace.rs and trace_ingest.rs existed, per the discipline that has already won
disagreements in 5d-ii, 9a and 9b. Where the implementation and this file disagree, this file
is the claim to argue against — not the thing to edit.
Every line number below was read out of trace/*.jsonl by hand and checked against the symbol
extents the index actually records, which are listed under `extents` so the reading is
_endpoints: An assertion is `caller_symbol TEST_OBSERVED_CALL callee_symbol`. The TEST IS NEVER AN
ENDPOINT: for the stack test_basic -> parse -> tokenize the tracer records two call events,
and naming test_basic as the source of the second would assert a call test_basic never made.
Which test observed an edge lives on the observation, in `environment.runs[].tests` and in

src/lex.py._module_body: lines 1-3 and 7-8 and 14-15 are inside no symbol

src/parse.py._module_body: lines 1-7 are inside no symbol; line 5 is the module-level tokenize() call
src/parse.py._nesting: line 26 is inside both Parser (bytes 437-641) and parse_all (bytes 535-641); the innermost rule must pick parse_all, whose byte span is shorter

bound._: trace/bound.jsonl, with __CONTENT_MERKLE__ replaced by the merkle the index recorded. 23 records: 8 accepted, 2 refused at the repository layer, 1 unresolved by the producer, 12 declaring an unsupported form.

edges.note: DEPTH 2 AND DEPTH 3. The source is `parse`, never a test. Two tests reach the same call site, so the schema's observation identity makes them ONE observation whose environment names both — see the disagreement recorded in the README.
depth 2 and depth 3, one call site, two tests
callee_line 24 is inside both Parser and parse_all; the innermost must win, so the callee is the METHOD and not the class
depth 2, both endpoints in one file; caller_line 26 is inside Parser too and must resolve to parse_all
the record carrying the unknown key `depth`. It is ACCEPTED and the unknown key counted, so this edge existing is the proof that an unknown record key costs one datum and not the record.

no_edge.note: no record names it. Absence of observation is not absence of a call, and it gets no edge in either direction.
named only by two `crashed-test`/`interrupted-run` limitation records, which state no located frame. A limitation is not an edge.
THE DEFECT THE PLAN CORRECTS. The tracer saw test_basic -> parse -> tokenize. There must be no edge from the test to tokenize, at any depth, ever.
same again: test_method reaches parse through parse_all, so parse_all is the caller

refused_records.record: caller src/parse.py:16 (inside reload_lex) -> callee src/lex.py:1 (the lex module body)
refused_records.note: a resolved caller reaching a frame no symbol contains. Refused and counted; the import continues.

refused_records.record: caller src/parse.py:5 (module-level DEFAULTS = tokenize(...)) -> callee src/lex.py:4
refused_records.note: the caller is checked first, so this record produces exactly one refusal even though it is the module body on one side only.
the producer says it could not locate the frame. Counted, never guessed at.

refused_records.record: the `depth` key on the test_lazy_import record
refused_records.note: ignored and counted; the record is still believed (contract policy: unknown HEADER keys reject, unknown RECORD keys are ignored).

limitations._: One record per member of the closed limitation vocabulary, so every counted form has a producing case in this fixture. That is the 10a lesson: a tally member with no producer is untested.

partial._: trace/partial.jsonl. completed_at is null and completion_state is `partial`, which is legal; the contradiction the contract rejects is `complete` with a null completed_at.
partial.note: every observation this artifact writes must say `partial`, in environment and in details. A partial run must never read as a complete one.

unverified._: trace/unverified.jsonl. Both state fields null: nothing could be checked.
unverified.note: `unverified` is a distinct third value and is NEVER reported as `bound`. Absence of verification is not verification of absence.

stale._: trace/stale.jsonl. A well-formed content merkle of 64 zeros, which matches no tree.
stale.note: reported, NOT refused (plan section 5). The artifact is about this repository — repository_root_name matches — so its evidence is kept and labelled.

merged._: bound.jsonl then partial.jsonl into one index. The two runs share one call site: src/parse.py:10 -> src/lex.py:4.

shared_site.note: the merged completion state is the WEAKEST of the contributing runs. One contributor did not finish, so the row must not read `complete`; environment.runs[] keeps each run's own state exactly.

vocabulary.note: RESOLVED, not DIRECT and not INFERRED. The artifact states the call outright — unlike coverage, where a rule concludes it — but it names a file and a line, so only the ENDPOINTS need resolving. That is exactly what Directness::Resolved means, and it is the value AST_RESOLVED uses.
